<meta>continues from previous page: ...resulting from the root 'hve' (to call), with the addition of the suffix 'ap' and the process of 'samprasarana' (the transformation of a semi-vowel into a vowel). 'Suktani' (well-spoken things) comes from the root 'vach' (to speak) with the 'kta' suffix in the sense of the past passive participle. The accent on the final syllable of the second member is derived from the rule 'supamanat kta' (after a word beginning with 'su'). 'Haryatam' comes from the root 'hary' (to desire or shine), belonging to the 'bhavadi' class.</meta>

When the deity for the 'upanshu' (whispered) sacrifice on the full moon is Agni and Soma, then the verse "Agni-Soma, who today..." serves as the 'anuvakya' (invitatory prayer). This has been indicated in the section titled "The deities have been spoken of" (in the Aitareya Brahmana 1.6). He now recites this second verse.

## Hymn Text

**Agni and Soma, whoever today offers this speech to you two.**
**Grant him great vitality, the growth of cattle, and good horses. 2**

->Pada-patha<-
**Agni-Soma. Who. Today. To you two. This. Speech. Honors.**
**To him. Grant. Good-vitality. Of cows. Growth. Good-horses. 2**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni and Soma**, the **sacrificer who today**, in this ritual, **honors this** speech in the form of praise **to you two**, for your sake, **to that** sacrificer, **grant growth** of **cows** or cattle. What kind of growth? **Good vitality**, meaning endowed with excellent power and capability, and **good horses**, meaning endowed with excellent horses. Regarding the form 'gavam' (of cows), although the rule 'savekach' would prescribe an accent on the case ending, the prohibition 'na goshvan savavarnai' maintains the original accent.

->He now recites the third verse.<-

## Hymn Text

**Agni and Soma, he who would offer an oblation to you, he who would perform the preparation of the offering.**
**He shall attain full life, with offspring and great vitality. 3**

->Pada-patha<-
**Agni-Soma. Who. Oblation. Who. To you two. Would offer. Offering-preparation.**
**He. With offspring. Good-vitality. All. Life. Attain. 3**

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Agni and Soma, the sacrificer who would offer** an oblation (specifically an oblation of clarified butter) **to you two**, or **he who would offer** a ritual preparation <note>original: "havishkritim"</note> made with offerings like the 'charu' (boiled rice) and 'purodasha' (sacrificial cake), **he**, the sacrificer, **shall attain** or reach **all** (the entirety of) **his life**, endowed with **offspring** (such as sons and grandsons) and **good vitality**. Regarding the form 'ahutim' (oblation), the root 'hu' (to sacrifice) with the suffix 'ktin' results in the retention of the original accent of the 'gati' (preverb/particle). 'Dashat' comes from the root 'dash' (to give), taking the 'at' augment in the 'let' (subjunctive) mood. Because it is linked to the relative pronoun 'ya', it does not undergo the 'nighata' (loss of accent). In 'havishkritim', where the 'havis' (offering) is the 'kriti' (doing or preparation), the rule of 'bahuvrihi' compound causes the first member to retain its original accent.
